wy_reaper_wall.blurb: Reaper Wall is a steep, tree-sheltered cliff in Devil's Kitchen, the North Fork Popo Agie canyon near Lander. All 18 routes are bolted sport lines and nearly all are hard: one at 5.11, five at 5.12, eleven at 5.13 and one at 5.14. The face is slightly overhanging and heavily featured, and it sits back from the canyon so it takes less wind than the walls beside it. The overhang makes falls long enough that it is a poor choice for kids and dogs. Reaching it means a scrambly walk down canyon from the Apocalypse walls, then a short climb back up to the ledge below the wall.

wy_upper_tier.blurb: The Upper Tier is the higher of two levels at Plumb Line Crag, a short walk beyond Citadel Crag in the Vedauwoo area outside Laramie. It is nearly all single-pitch trad, 17 of its 18 lines, plus one top rope. Climbs are short, roughly 20 to 110 feet, and mostly fall in the 5.10 to 5.11 range, with one or two easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range and a couple at 5.12. Expect cracks, seams and faces on granite with very few bolts, so bring a full rack and be ready to build your own anchors. It is much quieter than the better-known Vedauwoo formations, and wind dries the rock quickly after storms.

wy_wolf_point.blurb: Wolf Point is a big dolomite cliff in the Little Popo Agie canyon near Lander, known for steep, sustained, pocketed sport climbing. All 18 routes here are bolted, and the focus is hard: one 5.10, three 5.11s, three 5.12s and eleven at 5.13. The main feature is a long overhanging cave whose lines start from the ground, and many need a very long rope, around 80 meters. The face looks south, so it is hot in summer, though an arch and the shape of the cave give shade on the right in the morning and on the left later in the day. The walk in is long and steep, with a river crossing, and rattlesnakes are common.
wy_wolf_point.approach: A long, steep hike: switchbacks drop to a river crossing that can be risky in high water, then the trail traverses and climbs to the cave. Allow about 45 minutes.

wy_zorro_area.blurb: Zorro is a sport crag set apart from the main walls at Wild Iris, on Limestone Mountain above Lander. All 18 routes are bolted. Most fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with seven at 5.11, and a few easier lines in the 5.7 to 5.9 range, so it suits climbers working through the low and middle double digits. The climbing is on pocketed dolomite. The wall faces west, which means it sits in shade through the morning and gets sun later. The setting is quiet and scenic, looking over the valley toward the bigger crags and the distant Wind Rivers.

wy_amphitheater_the_2.blurb: The Amphitheater is a small, cave-like cliff in Rogers Canyon, a short drive from Laramie, on the north side of the road across from the Dark Side. All 17 routes are bolted sport climbs, and they lean hard: thirteen sit at 5.12, with three at 5.10 and one at 5.13. The routes are short and sharp, mostly gathered on the eastern half of the bowl with a few left of its arete. The left part of the wall is pale rock and the right is dark grey to black. It is a handy local crag for steep, powerful lines rather than a trip destination.

wy_b_rodeo_wave.blurb: Rodeo Wave is a hard-leaning section of the Main Wall at Wild Iris, southwest of Lander, and the second crag in from the left end. Most of the 17 climbs are bolted sport routes, with two boulder problems at V13 included. Sport grades start at one 5.10 and run mostly from 5.12 to 5.14, with six at 5.14. Expect short, powerful, pocketed dolomite that is steep and bouldery for its grade. The Main Wall faces south and sits in sun most of the day, though trees at its base give some shade and shelter. It is a poor pick for newer climbers, and thunderstorms are a real hazard on the open approach.

wy_c_east_sector.blurb: East Sector is the first crag you meet on the approach to Rock Springs Buttress, high above Jackson Hole near the resort. It holds 17 climbs of mixed character: mostly multi-pitch alpine-style lines, a pair of sport routes, one trad route and a couple of ice or mixed lines in winter. Rock climbs run from 5.10 into the low 5.13s, with the bulk at 5.10 and 5.12. Reaching the sector means following the main buttress approach to the talus beneath the Central Sector, then contouring east. Elevation is a little over 8,600 feet, so weather and chilly mornings are worth planning for.

wy_college_the.blurb: The College is a small sandstone sport crag in Green River, Wyoming, a quick stop for people passing along I-80. It has 17 climbs, mostly bolted, with a broad spread: an easy scramble or two, a few routes in the 5.8 to 5.9 range, a core of 5.10s and 5.11s, and a handful of 5.12s plus one boulder problem. Locals use it after work. Bolts are older, and some routes carry painted names and grades that have partly faded. Sandstone in the Green River area can be inconsistent, solid in one spot and crumbly a few feet away, so test holds as you go.

_conflicts.wy_c_east_sector: Stored rock amphibolite; the buttress page says granite (https://mountainproject.com/area/105833991/rock-springs-buttress). Aspect: East Sector page says mostly south (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/114587646/east-sector), buttress page says west-facing; no aspect added.
_conflicts.wy_amphitheater_the_2: Stored rock sandstone; Rogers Canyon page calls the canyon limestone (https://www.mountainproject.com/area/105840228/rogers-canyon).
_conflicts.wy_b_rodeo_wave: Stored dolomite; a third-party guide (https://app.advcollective.com/climbing/rodeo-wave-at-wild-iris-steep-sport-climbing-in-wyoming) says granite, Main Wall page says dolomite (https://mountainproject.com/area/106539357/the-main-wall).
